case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 16-2-2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2669 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain CJ: This appeal by cave is directed against the judgment and order sated 16-2-2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2669 of 1999 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the order dated 12-7-1998 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Satkhira in Title Appeal No.142 of 1994 rejecting the application praying for withdrawal of suit with leave to sue afresh.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this appeal, in a nutshell, are:

Respondent Nos. 1 to 15 as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.114 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Satkhira, praying for declaration of title and for further declaration that Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1992 filed before defendant-respondent No.2, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Satkhira, is illegal, collusive and without jurisdiction. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that defendant-respondent Nos.1-4 have no right to lease out the suit land. The rents of SA Khatian Nos.20, 21, 22 and 23 having fallen due, Certificate Case Nos.6 of 1980-1981, 12 of 1980-1981, 13 of 1980-1981 and 14 of 1980-1981 were filed by the Government and notices of the above cases were duly served and then after compliance with of all requirements the suit land was put to auction. On 5-5-1981, the land to be auctioned was purchased by plaintiff Nos.13, 5-8-9 and 10-13 and from them, plaintiff Nos.1, 9, 14 and 15 purchased some properties by different kabalas. Defendant No.2 illegally started the above Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1992 and hence the suit has been filed.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint of the suit, contending, inter-alia that the suit is barred by limitation. The original owner of the suit land left the country before 1965 and has been living in India permanently. In order to circumvent the Government from taking over possession of the above property as per provisions of President's Order No.98 of 1972, the aforesaid property was fraudulently shown to have been sold in auction. In fact, Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1992 was started for treating the property as khas property of the Government and one Ashrafuddin illegally got his name mutated in the khatian in respect of the suit land.

4. The trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 16-10-1994 dismissed the suit.

5. The plaintiff-respondent Nos.1 to 15 then preferred Title Appeal No.142 of 1994 before the learned District Judge, Satkhira, which was transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Satkhira, for disposal. In the said appeal, the plaintiffs filed an application under sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 1 of Order XXIII read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for withdrawal of the suit along with appeal with a permission to sue afresh on 15-9-1996. By the order dated 23-2-1997 the said application dated 15-9-1996 was rejected as not pressed. On 7-1-1999, the plaintiffs again filed an application under sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule I of Order XXIII read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for withdrawal of the suit and the appeal with leave to sue afresh. After herring, the appellate Court rejected the application on 7-1-1999.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court, the plaintiffs filed a revisional application bet ore the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.2669 of 1999. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 16-2-2002 made the Rule absolute.

7. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the defendants as the leave-petitioners have filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.98 of 2003 before this Division and obtained leave on 2-7-2005 resulting in Civil Appeal No.196 of 2005.

8. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellants, sub nits that formal defects in the suit were pointed out by the defendants at the initial stage even then the plaintiffs did not file any application for withdrawal of the suit and that on the other hand, the plaintiffs allowed the same to proceed and they also adduced evidence. Accordingly, they cannot be allowed to withdraw the suit to sue afresh, when by an order dated 23-2-1997 similar application dated 15-9-1996 praying for withdrawal of the suit with leave to sue afresh was rejected as being not pressed and, as such, the impugned judgment and order delivered by the High Court Division should be set-aside. He further submits that mere defect of the parties is not a formal defect and such defect can be cured by filing a petition for amendment and accordingly, the appellate Court did not find any ground of formal defect and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division without reversing the said finding of the appellate Court should be set-aside.

9. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents, on the other hand, submits that the judgment of the High Court Division in allowing the application for withdrawal of the suit and the appeal with the permission to sue afresh is based on proper appreciation of relevant provisions of law and the materials on record and, as such, no interference is called for. He further submits that the suit was bad for defect of parties and that the statements made in the plaint were not correct and that those statements could not be corrected by amendment and if such amendment is allowed the nature and character of the suit will be changed and, as such, the suit and the appeal should be allowed to be withdrawn with the leave of the Court for filing the same afresh.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Attorney-General for the appellants and the learned Advocate-on-Record for the respondents, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

11. Before embarking upon the conflicting submissions of the learned Attorney-General for the appellants and the learned Advocate-on-record for the respondents it would be proper to quote the g rounds, on which, leave was granted as follows:

"Though the formal defects in the suit were pointed out by the defendants at the initial stage the plaintiffs even then the plaintiffs, even being aware of the said defects, did not file any application for withdrawal of the suit and on the other hand allowed the same to proceed and they also adduced evidence and accordingly they cannot be allowed to withdraw the suit to sue afresh more so when by order dated 23-2-1997 similar application dated 15-9-1996 praying for withdrawal of the suit with leave was rejected as not being pressed and further mere defect of the parties is not a formal defect and such defect can be amended by filing a petition for amendment and accordingly, the appellate Court did not find any ground of formal defect but the High Court Division committed error of law in making the Rule absolute."

12. Admittedly, the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of title and for further declaration that he Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1992 filed before defendant No.2, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Satkhira, was illegal, collusive and without jurisdiction and that defendant Nos.1- have no right to lease out the said land.

13. Both the parties adduced evidence, oral and documentary. Having considered the evidence on record, the learned Senior Assistant judge dismissed the suit holding that it was barred 'rider section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that the auction sales were not genuine and that he suit land was the excess land of Ashrafuddin, by the judgment and decree dated 16-10-1994. Against the said judgment and decree, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No.142 of 1994 before the learned District Judge, Satkhira. The said appeal was transferred to the First Court of Additional District Judge, Satkhira for disposal. In the said appeal, on 15-9-1996, the plaintiffs filed an application under sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 1 of Order XXIII read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for withdrawal of Title Suit No.114 of 1993 and with the appeal with the permission to sue afresh.

14. For the better appreciation, we should have a glance over sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 1 of Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure:

"1.(1) At any time after the institution of a suit plaintiff may, as against all or any of the defendants, withdraw his suit or abandon part of his claim.

(2) Where the Court is satisfied—

(a) that a suit must fail by reason of some formal defect, or

(b) that there are other sufficient grounds for allowing the plaintiff to institute a fresh suit for the subject-matter of a suit or part of a claim, it may, on such terms as it thinks fit, grant the plaintiff permission to withdraw from such suit or abandon such part of a claim with liberty to institute a fresh suit in respect of the subject-matter of such suit or such part of a claim."

15. On 23-2-1997, the plaintiff-respondents filed an application stating that they would not press the application dated 15-9-1996 for withdrawal of the suit with the permission to sue afresh. Accordingly, the appellate Court rejected the said application by order No.37 dated 23-2-1997 as being not pressed and fixed the date of hearing of the appeal on 4-3-1997. On 7-1-1999, the plaintiff-respondents filed another application for withdrawal of Title Suit No.114 of 1993 along with the title appeal with the permission to sue afresh.

16. The plaintiff-respondents stated, inter alia, in the said application dated 7-1-1999 that the original suit was bad for defect of parties and that the wrong statements made in the original suit could not be corrected by amendment and that if the amendment is allowed the nature and character of the suit would be changed and, as such, they prayed for withdrawal of the original suit and the appeal with the permission to sue afresh. The appellate Court by the order No.61 dated 12-7-1999 rejected the application for withdrawal holding that defendant Nos.1-4 did not raise any objection that the suit was bad for defect of parties and, as such, the learned Senior Assistant Judge did not give any finding that Title Suit No.114 of 1993 was bad for defect of parties. The appellate Court also came to the finding that the plaintiff-respondents filed the first application dated 15-9-1996 incorporating two grounds under sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule 1 of Order XXIII read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected as being not pressed on 23-2-1997. The appellate Court then came to the finding that the present application dated 7-1-1999 incorporating one more ground for withdrawal of the suit was not maintainable and, as such, the said application was rejected on 12-7-1999.

17. The High Court Division, on the other hand, came to the finding that the plaintiffs were quite, conscious of the formal defects from long before the delivery of the judgment and drawing up of the decree by the trial Court. They took no steps under rule 1 of Order XXIII at that stage and slept over the matter. The High Court Division further came to the finding that the plaintiffs having contested the suit with full knowledge adducing evidence and losing the suit on merits could not be allowed to withdraw the same with liberty to sue afresh because that would be contrary to the letter and spirit of sub-rule (2) of rule 1 of Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure.

18. Upon making the aforesaid findings, the High Court Division made contradictory finding holding that under sub-rule (1) of rule 1 of Order XXIII, the plaintiffs are at liberty to withdraw the suit without any ground and that an order permitting withdrawal of the suit and at the same time, refusing leave to institute a fresh suit did not seem to be contemplated by sub-rule (2) and was not a proper order passed by the appellate Court. The High Court Division further held that the Court has ample discretion to reject an application filed under sub-rule (2) but if it allows withdrawal, it could not refuse leave to bring a fresh suit for the obvious reason that the sole purpose for which withdrawal was sought was to institute a fresh suit. The High Court Division, therefore, allowed the application for withdrawal of the suit with the permission to sue afresh setting aside the order dated 12-7-1999 passed by the appellate Court.

19. Having lone through the impugned judgment, we find that the High Court Division made contradictory findings while making the Rule absolute. The High Court Division came to the finding that withdrawal should not be allowed with the permission to sue afresh but on the other hand came to the finding that since rule 1 of Order XXIII allows withdrawal with permission to sue afresh, the application could not be rejected.

20. We do not approve of such contradictory findings of the High Court Division while allowing the application for withdrawal of the suit and the appeal with the permission to sue afresh. The High Court Division committed gross illegality in holding that sub-rule (1) of Order XXIII allows the plaintiffs to withdraw the suit without any ground and, as such, filing of fresh suit under sub-rule (2) cannot be stopped, sub-rule (2) of Order XXIII is independent of sub-rule (1) and these sub-rules cannot be read together. The purposes of the said two sub-rules are quite different.

21. The provisions as to withdrawal of this suit laid down in this rule are as follows:

(i) As per sub-rule (1) of rule 1 the plaintiff can withdraw his suit or abandon part of his claim as a matter of right without the permission of the court. But in such case he will be precluded from suing again on the same cause of action. (Baidyanath vs Shyama Sunday, AIR 1943 Cal 427)

(ii) Under sub-rule (2) the plaintiff may, in the circumstances mentioned therein, be permitted by the court to withdraw from a suit with liberty to sue afresh on the same cause of action. (Sasson vs Ardeshir, AIR 1926 Bom 189)

22. We have already noticed that the plaintiff-respondents filed the first application dated 15-9-1996 incorporating two grounds and that they filed the second application incorporating one more ground which is as under:

"মূল মামলাটি পক্ষদোষে দুষ্ট থাকে এবং মূল মামলার স্টেটমেন্ট সঠিক না থাকায় এবং উক্ত বিষয়গুলি আদৌ সংশোধনী যোগ্য না হওয়ায় বা সংশোধন করা হইলে মূল মামলার আরজির চরিত্র বিষয় পরিবর্তন হওয়ায় প্রেক্ষাপটে মূল মামলার পুনঃদাখিলের শর্তে অত্র আপীলসহ মূল মামলা উহ্য করিয়া লওয়া আবশ্যিক হইতেছে।"

23. Having gone through the third ground for withdrawal of the suit, we find that the plaintiffs took the plea that the suit was bad for defect of parties and that the statements made in the suit were not correct and those statements could not be corrected by way of amendment and that if such amendments were allowed the nature of the suit would be changed and, as such, the original suit and the appeal should be allowed to be withdrawn with the permission to sue afresh.

24. By its order dated 12-7-1999, the appellate Court came to the finding that defendant Nos.1-4 did not raise any objection about defect of parties in their written objection and that Senior Assistant Judge while delivering the judgment and decree in Title Suit No.114 of 1993 did not state anything about defect of parties in the suit. If the plaintiffs find that more parties are required to be added they could do so by filing an application for addition of party and for that purpose it was not necessary for withdrawal of the suit. Moreover, defect of parties cannot be a ground for withdrawal of the suit.

25. The plaintiffs in ground No.3 further stated that statements made in the plaint of the original suit are not correct and that those statements could not be corrected by way of amendment and if the amendment is allowed the nature and character of the suit would be changed. This plea of the plaintiffs also does not stand to reason. If there are wrong statements in the plaint that may be corrected at any stage of the suit by filing an application for amendment. If such amendment is allowed the question of changing the nature and character of the suit will not arise at all.

26. Having considered the submissions of the learned Attorney-General for the appellants and the learned Advocate-on-record for the respondents and on consideration of the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division and the materials on record, we are of the view that in order to prolong litigation, the plaintiffs have taken recourse to dilatory tactics.

27. A party should not be granted permission to withdraw the appeal as well as the suit unless it is clearly established that the suit as well as the appeal is bound to fail on a mere formal defect which could not be rectified by the plaintiff under normal ordinary circumstances and the interest of justice requires that such permission 'should be granted. (Dacca Municipal Committee vs Md Rafiqul Islam, 25 DLR 97)

28. In the case in hand, we have already held that the plea of defect of parties was not taken by the defendants and if the plaintiffs feel one or more parties are required to be added they could do so by way of amendment. In addition, the plea of the plaintiffs that there are wrong statements in the plaint and that if amendment is allowed to correct the wrong statements, the nature and character of the suit will be changed. This plea does not stand to reason because the wrong statements made in the plaint can be corrected by way of amendment which will not change the nature and character of the suit. The plaintiffs may also pray for consequential relief by way of amendment on payment of ad valorem court fee and for addition of such relief, withdrawal of the suit and appeal with the permission to sue afresh is not at all necessary.

29. The application for withdrawal of the suit having not stated specifically the legal, formal or other defects which cannot be cured even by amendment of the plaint and the assertions made therein being vague and in lump, the order for withdrawal with liberty to sue afresh is set-aside. (Abdur Rahman vs Abdul Mobin, 46 DLR 246).

30. Therefore, we find that the judgment of the High Court Division allowing the application for withdrawal of the suit and the appeal with the permission to sue afresh should be set-aside. The plaintiff-respondents could not make out a case for withdrawal as contemplated under sub-rules (1) and (2) of rule I of Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure.

In the light of the findings made before, we find substance in this appeal. Accordingly, this civil appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is set-aside and the appellate Court is directed to dispose of the appeal as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

End.
